[Exhibitions > Budućnosti na dodir > 14 Jan 2025 - 31 Dec 2026 / MSU, 2. kat]

The **Museum of Contemporary Art** (Croatian: *Muzej suvremene umjetnosti*, often abbreviated to **MSU**) is a contemporary art museum located on Dubrovnik Avenue in Zagreb, Croatia. It is the biggest and most modern museum in the country.\[5]\[6] Vesna Meštrić is current director of MSU, replacing Zdenka Badovinac in late 2023 first temporarily and as of 2024 officially.\[7]

[Museum of Contemporary Art, Zagreb - Wikipedia > Architecture]

In 1998, a decision was made to move the museum to a brand new building on the corner of Dubrovnik and Većeslav Holjevac avenues in Novi Zagreb district.

A competition for the building's design was held, and architect Igor Franić's design was chosen out of 85 entries submitted. The cornerstone for the new building was laid in November 2003, and the new museum finally opened on 11 December 2009, after six years of construction which was beset with several delays. [About us]

The Museum of Contemporary Art Zagreb was founded in 1954 under the name City Gallery of Contemporary Art. The goal of this institution was to promote and collect recently produced artworks of younger generations which, among others, encompassed the achievements of the Exat 51 group – Ivan Picelj, Vjenceslav Richter, Aleksandar Srnec, Božidar Rašica, Vlado Kristl and others – artists who advocated geometric abstraction, developing forth the heritage of historical avant-garde. In the fifties the Museum organized the first travelling exhibitions of abstract art (*Didactic Exhibition: Abstract Art*) and had an important role in drawing the attention of culturally interested public to international modern and contemporary art. By the end of the fifties, the artist group GORGONA (Josip Vaništa, Ivan Kožarić, Julije Knifer, Marijan Jevšovar, Đuro Seder…), “the last European avant-garde group” as it was later labeled by international critics, initiated their activities under the auspices of the Museum.

The Museum moved into the new building in December 2009. The specific MSU Collections, formed during a period of half a century at the cultural border between the East and the West, rich exhibition and educative programs, archives, library, audio-visual centre, multimedia hall and many other facilities are now accessible to Croatian and international public."],"code":"SUCCESS"}},{"url":"https://mdc.hr/en/","title":"MDC - Museum documentation center","description":"The Croatian Natural History Museum is organizing the Congress “180 Years of Dedication to Natural History Heritage – A Museum for the Future”, to mark the 180th anniversary of the Museum’s founding. more ... [Exhibitions > Budućnosti na dodir > 14 Jan 2025 - 31 Dec 2026 / MSU, 2. kat]

Muzej suvremene umjetnosti nastavlja obogaćivati muzejski postav s taktilnim modelima namijenjenima slijepim i slabovidnima osobama – ali i svima željnima taktilnog doživljaja umjetnosti. Projekt *Budućnosti na dodir* nastavak je i proširenje uspješnog projekta *MSU na dodir*, koji Muzej suvremene umjetnosti provodi s ciljem obogaćivanja ponude za slijepe i slabovidne osobe, ali i sve one koji žele taktilno istraživati muzejske predmete. Taktilni modeli umjetničkih djela nastali u sklopu ovog pokreta i producirani u okviru projekta *MSU na dodir* imaju tako dvojaku funkciju – ne samo da omogućuju posjetiteljima interaktivno istraživanje umjetnosti, već i pomažu revitalizirati izvorni smisao tih djela, jer je fizička interakcija i otvorenost djela – gdje posjetitelj svojom akcijom dopunjava i mijenja djela – bila temeljna ideja mnogih radova ovog pokreta.

Founded in 1954, the MSU is one of the world’s oldest museums specializing in contemporary art. The “Collection as a Verb” exhibition currently includes three ongoing exhibitions (“Futures”, “Friendship”, “Sad Songs of War”) and a series of smaller current exhibitions in the Triggers cycle, representing an impressive holdings organized into 15 collections and donations. The museum also organizes retrospectives, thematic, international and other exhibitions. Annually, the MSU holds 250-300 programs in the fields of visual art, film, music, performance, theater, etc. Internationally active from the beginning, the MSU has been a member of L’Internationale since 2023, an alliance of 15 European contemporary art institutions that are developing the joint project “Museum of the Commons”. [About us]

The Museum of Contemporary Art Zagreb was founded in 1954 under the name City Gallery of Contemporary Art. The goal of this institution was to promote and collect recently produced artworks of younger generations which, among others, encompassed the achievements of the Exat 51 group – Ivan Picelj, Vjenceslav Richter, Aleksandar Srnec, Božidar Rašica, Vlado Kristl and others – artists who advocated geometric abstraction, developing forth the heritage of historical avant-garde. In the fifties the Museum organized the first travelling exhibitions of abstract art (*Didactic Exhibition: Abstract Art*) and had an important role in drawing the attention of culturally interested public to international modern and contemporary art. By the end of the fifties, the artist group GORGONA (Josip Vaništa, Ivan Kožarić, Julije Knifer, Marijan Jevšovar, Đuro Seder…), “the last European avant-garde group” as it was later labeled by international critics, initiated their activities under the auspices of the Museum.

The Museum moved into the new building in December 2009. The specific MSU Collections, formed during a period of half a century at the cultural border between the East and the West, rich exhibition and educative programs, archives, library, audio-visual centre, multimedia hall and many other facilities are now accessible to Croatian and international public.
